basics.name: José Miguel Elizalde Moncayo
basics.title: Senior Data Engineer
basics.summary: Computer Science Engineer focused on data engineering, cloud data platforms and analytics.

projects.name: Utility client — Weather Alert application (San Diego, CA)
projects.summary: Map-based alerting app that ingests planned, unplanned and potential power outages every 5 minutes, runs calculations and raises alerts shown on the map.
bullets: Cut the main ingestion pipeline's average runtime from about 6 minutes to 50 seconds (roughly 86% faster).

Led the migration off Amazon Pinpoint to Amazon SES and AWS End User Messaging, driven by EventBridge and Lambda: researched replacement services, designed the target architecture, broke the work into stories and led implementation with the other developers.
Consolidated the application from two separate AWS accounts into one.
Took on backend and platform engineering beyond the data role: API work in TypeScript with NestJS, and infrastructure as code with Terraform.
Own ongoing maintenance and bug fixing across the ingestion, processing and alerting pipeline.

work.summary: Built end-to-end analytics projects for clients across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, often solo or with one data analyst: infrastructure, pipelines, data warehouses and dashboards.
bullets: Led projects independently or with a small team, from scoping to delivery.
Worked directly with clients as a business developer: gathered needs, presented solutions and delivered outcomes.

projects.name: Wine retail company
projects.summary: Built and deployed the AWS infrastructure for an analytics platform covering Sales, Finance and Marketing.
bullets: Analytics pipeline: ingested multiple sources into S3, loaded them into Redshift with Glue, modeled them with DBT and reported in QuickSight.
Machine learning pipeline: fed Redshift data into SageMaker notebooks and Amazon Personalize recommendation models.
Automation: sent personalized recommendation emails to customers with Amazon SES based on Personalize output.
Cut data warehouse build time by 50% and raw data processing time by 90%.

projects.name: Furniture retail company #2
projects.summary: Led a Google Cloud analytics solution for Sales and Inventory.
bullets: Pipeline: connected Google Sheets to BigQuery and pulled Shopify data through its API with Python.
Data warehouse: modeled the warehouse in BigQuery with DBT.
Visualization: built Looker dashboards for the client.

projects.name: Furniture retail company #1
projects.summary: Built a Google Cloud analytics solution for Sales, Inventory and Finance data.
bullets: Pipeline: extracted data from an on-premises SQL Server with Python into BigQuery.
Data warehouse: modeled the warehouse in BigQuery with DBT.
Visualization: connected Power BI to BigQuery for near-real-time reporting.

Pipeline: connected Retool to Google Cloud and built the warehouse with DBT.
Visualization: Looker dashboards for sales and inventory per machine.

work.summary: Data support for the Customer Success organization.
bullets: Resolved Jira requests for dashboards, SQL analysis and pipeline automation; designed and optimized Looker dashboards.
Ran internal audits to find malpractice in Customer Success teams and retrained them on the platform.

bullets: Met with stakeholders to gather requirements and present the new Power BI reports.
Built data models in Snowflake on top of Azure Data Lake to feed the new dashboards.

bullets: Built a pipeline from Excel files and SQL Server into an SQL star-schema warehouse.
Created Power BI dashboards on business performance during the pandemic.

work.summary: Analyzed ticket-resolution and agent-performance metrics for an IT support company.
bullets: Built interactive Tableau dashboards for ticket-resolution KPIs.

personalProjects.name: Sleeper API Analyzer
personalProjects.summary: Fantasy football lineup optimizer that pulls rosters from the Sleeper API and matchup data from ESPN to pick the best weekly lineup and recommend player swaps.
bullets: Scores players by blending projections (50%), opponent matchup strength from ESPN defense ranks (40%) and recent form (10%).
Builds lineups in four phases: lock fixed-position starters, fill FLEX slots across positions, fill the bench, then suggest swaps when the score gap passes a configurable threshold.
Caches API responses, supports per-league configuration and tier cutoffs, and outputs to the terminal or a Markdown report; covered by a pytest suite.
Built with Claude as an AI pair programmer.
